previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and GERD was admitted for fevers and myalgias. He presented with a temperature of 101°F and diffuse muscle pain, likely due to an influenza-like illness. Given his immunosuppressed state, he was started on empiric Tamiflu. Initial labs showed elevated liver enzymes, which persisted despite resolution of fever. Blood and urine cultures were negative, and imaging showed no acute findings. A liver biopsy revealed mild acute cellular rejection, prompting an increase in sirolimus from 2 mg to 3 mg daily. His symptoms resolved, and he was discharged home with plans for follow-up labs, an MRCP, and hepatitis B vaccination. During admission, he was also diagnosed with type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.7%) and advised on dietary management.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  History of chronic kidney disease and cryptogenic cirrhosis with
increased LFTs.  Please evaluate for an infectious process.

COMPARISONS:  Multiple chest radiographs dated back to ___ PA
and lateral radiograph of the chest.

FINDINGS:  The lungs are clear without evidence of focal consolidations
concerning for pneumonia.  There is no pneumothorax. There is a small right
pleural effusion.  Heart size is normal.  The hilar and mediastinal contours
are normal.  The visualized osseous structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No focal consolidations concerning for infection identified. New
small right pleural effusion.

HISTORY:  Status post liver transplant ___ years ago with new transaminitis. 
Chronic kidney disease.  Evaluate for portal vein thrombosis, liver pathology,
and renal pathology.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale and color spectral Doppler imaging of the liver was
performed.  Ultrasound imaging of the kidneys was performed as well.

COMPARISON:  MRCP from ___.

FINDINGS:

Abdomen: 

There is atrophy of the left lobe of the liver with chronically dilated bile
ducts, which appears similar to prior MRCP, compatible with chronically
stenosed ducts.  The liver echotexture is otherwise within normal limits.  No
intrahepatic mass is visualized.  The pancreas is not well visualized.  

There is normal color spectral doppler waveforms in the portal vein, hepatic
artery, and hepatic veins.  Of note, in the main hepatic artery, the peak
systolic velocity is up to 124 centimeters/second, which is at the upper level
limit of normal.  

The spleen measures 8.3 cm in size.  There is no ascites.  

Kidneys: 

The right kidney is small, measuring 9.1 cm.  Normal echogenicity.  The left
kidney is normal in appearance, measuring 10.5 cm.  

IMPRESSION:

1.  Patent portal vein. 

2.  Stable, mildly dilated bile ducts in the left lobe of the liver with
associated atrophy, suggesting chronic stenosed bile ducts. 

3.  No evidence of hydronephrosis bilaterally.  The right kidney is smaller
than the left.

HISTORY:  PICC placement.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, there has been placement of a
right subclavian PICC line that extends to the mid portion of the SVC. 
Cardiac silhouette is essentially within normal limits and there is no
evidence of vascular congestion, pleural effusion, or acute focal pneumonia.
